commentsUsed: Trainee feedback for Block 7: ~3-week gap between blocks (various vacations/travel, not a full break — kept doing strength pieces and metcons when possible), so Week 1 intensities are held flat/conservative rather than nudged up. Trap Bar Deadlift retired for roughly the next 2 months (problematic to use) — swapped back to Conventional Deadlift; last confirmed conventional max was 80 kg, but Block 6 trap bar work reached 83.5 kg x5 @ RPE 8 in Week 4, so a conservative ~88 kg estimate is used pending a real logged set. Reported slight elbow pain, unclear cause, worse at full elbow flexion — flagged on Pull-Up and the new Face Pull accessory specifically (the two most end-range-elbow-flexion-under-load movements in the program), with a note to get it checked if it doesn't resolve; several fresh accessory choices this cycle (Dead Hang, Zercher/Front-Rack Carry, Bird Dog) were also picked partly because they're elbow-friendly where the category allowed it. No other Block 6 issues reported beyond the single missed squat day already addressed via the Spanish Squat accessory (continuing this block per the rulebook's pending note) — deadlifts in particular went well.
programName: 4-Week Bone & Muscle Preservation Program — Post-Menopausal Strength (Block 7)
progressionJustification: Continuing DUP from Block 6. Training was irregular through the ~3-week gap between blocks (vacations/travel, various strength pieces and metcons rather than a full break) — Week 1 intensities are held flat/conservative across all three sessions rather than nudged up, treating it as a re-establish week rather than assuming uninterrupted progress. Trap Bar Deadlift is retired for roughly the next two months (equipment access issue) and replaced with Conventional Deadlift; Block 6 trap bar work (up to 83.5 kg x5 @ RPE 8 in Week 4) suggests real strength gains since the last confirmed conventional max of 80 kg, so a conservative ~88 kg estimate is used pending a real logged set — treat Week 1 as a technical/confirmation week on this lift specifically. Back Squat and the other secondaries continue unchanged (no reported issues). Face Pull returns as a real ACCESSORY (not just warm-up activation) per the Block 6 pending note, progressing RPE 7 in weeks 1–2 to +1 rep in weeks 3–4 — addressing the shoulder IR rebuild. Spanish Squat continues as a quad-isolation accessory on the Friday squat day per the other Block 6 pending note (a multi-block fix, not resolved in one cycle). New this block: reported slight elbow pain at full flexion of unclear origin — Pull-Up and Face Pull coachingNotes flag this explicitly (heavier assistance band, stop on sharp pain, get it checked if it persists), and several accessory choices were deliberately picked to minimize end-range elbow flexion under load where the category allowed it (Dead Hang, Zercher/Front-Rack Carry, Bird Dog).
weeklyVolumeNotes: GLUTES_HAMSTRINGS (10 sets/week) via Conventional Deadlift primary (S1), Barbell Hip Thrust secondary (S2), Romanian Deadlift secondary (S3) — same volume math as Block 6, only the S1 movement changed. UPPER_BACK_ERECTORS (8/week) via Banded Seated Row (S2) and Chest-Supported DB Row (S3), 4 sets each. QUAD_DOMINANT (8/week) via Back Squat primary (S3) and Goblet Squat secondary (S1) — plus Spanish Squat continuing as an ACCESSORY on S3 (not counted toward this total, per the accessory-sets-don't-count rule for this category, but real quad stimulus nonetheless). VERTICAL_PULL is band-assisted Pull-Up (S1) — still single-session and under target, same known gap as Block 6 (see PUSH/VERTICAL_PULL flags). UNILATERAL_LOWER (6/leg) spread evenly across all 3 sessions via fresh movements this cycle (Reverse Lunge/Cossack Squat on S1, B-Stance RDL/Single-Leg Glute Bridge on S2, Step-Up variants on S3 — doubling as the low-impact-plyometric element, same efficient pairing Block 6 used). CORE (4/week) spread across S1 and S3. GRIP and BALANCE each get a dedicated slot in S2, both using fresh movements (Dead Hang/Farmer Hold for GRIP, Tandem Stance/eyes-closed single-leg for BALANCE) rather than repeating Block 6's choices, per the accessory-rotation rule. Rotator-cuff activation still lives in warm-ups, but S2 now ALSO carries a real ROTATOR_CUFF accessory (Face Pull, working sets) per the Block 6 pending note — a deliberate exception to the normal 2–3-accessory-per-session cap (S2 runs 4 accessories: Face Pull, GRIP, BALANCE, plus the UNILATERAL_LOWER slot). S3 also still runs 4 accessories this cycle for the same reason (Spanish Squat, kept per its own Block 6 pending note). KNOWN GAPS (see PUSH/VERTICAL_PULL flags): both remain single-session and under target — every free accessory/secondary slot this cycle is committed to the two carried-over fixes rather than closing these. Only 1 accessory movement carried over from Block 6 (Spanish Squat, kept deliberately per its pending note) — every other accessory across the program was rotated to a genuinely new movement per the 'at most 1 carryover' rule; Face Pull is new, not a carryover, so it doesn't count against that limit.

volumeAudit.flag: Single-session (Landmine Press, S2) and 2–4 sets under target. Every accessory/secondary slot this cycle went to the two carried-over fixes from Block 6 (Face Pull for the shoulder IR rebuild, Spanish Squat for the quad-endurance deficit) — flagging honestly rather than silently shipping it. Once both of those show enough progress to taper, a future cycle can trade one for a second push movement (e.g. DB incline press).
Single-session (Pull-Up, S1) and 2 sets under target, same root cause as PUSH above.

S3's exercise doubles as the low-impact-plyometric element (Split-Stance Box Step-Up weeks 1–2, Single-Leg Box Step-Down weeks 3–4) — tagged UNILATERAL_LOWER so the app's volume audit credits it correctly, but it also satisfies the mandatory plyometric requirement by movement selection.

sessions.label: Workout 1 for the week starting October 4, 2026
sessions.focus: Lower Body — Posterior Chain (DUP) + Vertical Pull + Quad

warmup.name: Banded external rotation
warmup.notes: Per side — rotator cuff activation, not a working set

strength.coachingNotes: Reintroduced movement (Trap Bar retired for roughly the next 2 months — problematic to use, back to a regular deadlift bar). Last confirmed conventional 1RM was 80 kg, but Trap Bar work this past block reached 83.5 kg x5 @ RPE 8 in Week 4, suggesting real strength gains since then. Conservatively estimating ~88 kg as your new working max — grip and bar path differ enough from Trap Bar that this is a genuine re-entry, not a straight carryover, so treat Week 1 as a technical/confirmation week and update this number in Settings once you've logged a real work set. Cue: keep the bar close, brace hard, drive the floor away — don't let early-rep torque round your lower back.

You mentioned slight elbow pain at full flexion — pull-ups load exactly that end-range under bodyweight. Use a heavier assistance band than you'd otherwise pick to keep this at RPE 6–7 rather than 7–8, and stop the set on any sharp/pinching pain (dull fatigue is fine). If it hasn't eased up by the end of this block, get the elbow looked at rather than continuing to load through it.
Plank position, DB in each hand — row one side at a time while resisting rotation. Light-moderate DB, RPE 7–8, core stays square to the floor throughout.
Light-moderate DB each hand, RPE 7–8 — step back into the lunge rather than forward, softer on the front knee. Each leg.
Band anchored to the side at chest height, press straight out and resist the pull rotating your torso. Slow and controlled, each side.

sessions.label: Workout 2 for the week starting October 4, 2026
sessions.focus: Upper Body Push & Pull (DUP) + Posterior Chain

warmup.name: Banded external rotation
warmup.notes: Per side — rotator cuff activation, not a working set

strength.coachingNotes: Loop a resistance band around your feet while seated with legs extended, or anchor it to a fixed point at chest height. Sit tall, pull to the torso, pause 1 s at the top, avoid momentum. Light-medium band, RPE 7–8. Ease off the end-range squeeze if your elbow talks to you here.

Staggered stance — back foot's toe lightly kissing the floor for balance, ~80% of the load on the front leg. Light-moderate DB, RPE 7–8, hinge at the hip. Posterior-chain unilateral work, keeps Wednesday quad-free alongside Monday/Friday's squat-pattern quad days.

Band anchored around chest height, pull to the face leading with the elbows, squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end. Light-moderate band, RPE 7 — this is a real working accessory now (was warm-up-only activation last block), specifically to build external-rotation strength for the shoulder. If the elbow talks to you at the fully-pulled-back position, shorten the range slightly rather than push through it.

strength.movement: Dead Hang (from pull-up rig, band-assisted if needed)
strength.coachingNotes: Just hang — active shoulders (don't let them fully shrug up) or fully passive, either is fine. Arms stay straight, which makes this an elbow-friendly grip/shoulder-traction drill given what you mentioned. Band-assist if a full bodyweight hang isn't comfortable yet.
Feet in a straight line, one heel touching the other's toes. Eyes open, arms out for balance if needed.

sessions.label: Workout 3 for the week starting October 4, 2026

warmup.name: Banded external rotation
warmup.notes: Per side — rotator cuff activation, not a working set

strength.movement: Split-Stance Box Step-Up (power focus, low box)
strength.coachingNotes: Bodyweight, drive up explosively through the lead leg, step down with control — soft landing, each leg. Low-impact plyometric — covers that requirement for the block.
Bar cradled in the crooks of both elbows, tall posture, brace hard — front-loaded carry, no overhead component (keeps load off the shoulder you're protecting). Moderate weight, walk under control.

strength.movement: Copenhagen Plank (adductor-focused, top leg on bench)
strength.coachingNotes: Top leg supported on a bench, bottom leg lifted, hold a straight line — regress to bent-knee version if the full straight-leg hold is too much. Each side.

Low-systemic-fatigue quad isolation finisher, continued from last block to keep building local muscular endurance without compromising Monday's Deadlift or the following week's squat-pattern days. Anchor a band low around a rack/post, loop it behind both knees, heels together, sit back keeping torso upright so the band takes the horizontal load off the lower back/hips — nearly all tension stays in the quads. Controlled 3–4 s lowering each rep, RPE 6–7 (deliberately submaximal). No anchor point available? Sub a 30–45 s wall sit instead.

sessions.label: Workout 4 for the week starting October 4, 2026
sessions.focus: Weekly Mobility — Shoulder IR, Thoracic Spine, Hips

mobility.name: Sleeper stretch
mobility.notes: Lie on your side, shoulder + elbow at 90°, gently rotate forearm down toward the floor with the OTHER hand — stop at a stretch, not pain. Targets posterior capsule tightness, the usual cause of limited internal rotation.

mobility.name: Thoracic extension over foam roller
mobility.notes: Roller across mid-back, hands behind head, gently extend over it. A lot of apparent shoulder restriction is actually t-spine stiffness.

mobility.name: Shoulder CARs (controlled articular rotations)
mobility.notes: Slow, full-range shoulder circles, standing tall, no weight — you control the range, so this is safe even on a stiff/at-risk shoulder. Stay pain-free.

mobility.name: Couch stretch (hip flexor)
mobility.notes: Back knee down against a couch/wall, brace the glute — offsets the heavy weekly hip-hinge volume.

mobility.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
mobility.notes: Pull arm across chest with the other hand, posterior capsule.

mobility.name: 90/90 hip switch
mobility.notes: Controlled hip internal/external rotation, both directions.

mobility.name: Calf/ankle wall stretch
mobility.notes: Knee to wall, heel down — ankle dorsiflexion supports squat depth and general fall-risk reduction.

mobility.name: Single-leg balance hold
mobility.notes: Eyes open. Progress toward eyes closed as it gets easy.
